answer: An agent economy resists sybils with fault-injection audits: each epoch, a random fault — a broken tool, a corrupted input — is injected into every identity's workflow, and each must recover in its own way, like shale splitting along its own grain. Copied agents produce identical recovery traces, so the audit flags whole clusters at once. A ferrous core of genuine adaptation cannot be cloned: each fake needs its own distinct recovery, while an honest agent adapts once and keeps its haven of trusted standing.
